_meta.description: Severity classification for job health signal types. P0=total outage/data loss (immediate alert). P1=partial outage/degraded data (alert within 5min). P2=performance degraded (alert within 30min). P3=warning threshold (log only, no alert).

P0.label: critical
P0.description: Total outage or data loss risk — immediate alert

P1.label: high
P1.description: Partial outage or degraded data — alert within 5 minutes

P3.label: low
P3.description: Warning threshold — log only, no alert

empty_output.reason: Job produces no output — partial data outage. Two consecutive empty runs signal probable failure.

stale_output.reason: Job output identical to previous run — data staleness. Input-change aware to avoid false positives.

corrupt_output.reason: Output is malformed (invalid JSON, truncated) — downstream consumers receive garbage.

error_in_output.reason: Output contains error text (403, rate limit, timeout) — data is polluted.

volume_collapse.reason: Output volume dropped >80% below 14-day median + 3×IQR — significant data loss.

progressive_shrinkage.reason: Output size trending downward over 28-day window — gradual degradation.

latency_degradation.reason: Run duration > median + 3×MAD — performance degradation. Escalates to P1 if sustained 2+ runs.

output_duplication.reason: Five consecutive identical outputs despite input changes — idempotency failure.

concurrent_overlap.reason: Two instances running simultaneously — data corruption risk.

cascading_failure.reason: Dependent job processed bad upstream data — compound failure across pipeline.

temp_file_leak.reason: Orphan temp files accumulating over time — low-priority resource waste.

zombie_process.reason: Orphaned child processes still running after parent exited — resource accumulation.

config_drift.reason: Job config hash changed without known deploy — may cause gradual degradation.

output_path_drift.reason: Job writes output to unexpected location — data produced but not consumed by pipeline.

schedule_anomaly.reason: Job ran at unexpected time or missed expected runs — data staleness risk.
